## 1. Interactive Map (GPU Rendered)
The container below will host the map instance managed by `WebGeoDS.Map`.

<div id="map-canvas" style="height: 400px; width: 100%; border: 1px solid #30363d; border-radius: 8px; background: #0d1117;"></div>

## 2. Execution Console (Bilingual)
The CodeMirror 6-based code editor will be initialized in this space.



```{ojs}
//| echo: false

// ============================================================
// 1. Map Initialization (map.js)
// ============================================================
myMap = {
  const mapInstance = new WebGeoDS.Map("map-canvas", {
    center: [12.4964, 41.9028], // Centered on Rome
    zoom: 5
  });
  return mapInstance;
}
```



```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// ============================================================
// 2. Code Cell Initialization (code-cell.js)
// ============================================================
viewof pyCell = {
  const cell = new WebGeoDS.CodeCell({
    language: "Python",
    initialCode: "# Spatial analysis with Geopandas...\nprint('Starting...')",
    onRun:
      async (code, output) => {
        output.waiting("⌛ Processing...");
        // result() takes care of printing stdout and returning the spatial GeoJSON
        return  output.result(
          await WebGeoDS.Python.run(
            code,
            { packages: ["geopandas", "shapely"] }
          )
        );
      }
  });
  return cell.element;
}

```


```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// ============================================================
// 2. Code Cell Initialization (code-cell.js)
// ============================================================
viewof rCell = {
  const cell = new WebGeoDS.CodeCell({
    language: "R",
    initialCode: "# Spatial analysis with Geopandas...\nprint('Starting...')",
    onRun:
      async (code, output) => {
        output.waiting("⌛ Processing...");

        // result() takes care of printing stdout and returning the spatial GeoJSON
        return output.result(
          await WebGeoDS.R.run(
            code
            ,{ packages: ["sf"] }
          )
        );
      }
  });
  return cell.element;
}
```

```{ojs}
// This cell re-executes itself ONLY when the student clicks "▶ Run"!
// pyCell directly contains the GeoJSON [stdout, result] destructured from the v2 wrapper.
{
  if (pyCell) {
    const data = JSON.parse(pyCell);
    myMap.setGeoJSON("buffer-layer", data);
    myMap.fitToData(data, { padding: 60 });
  }
}
```

---

### How the four modules work together in this test

1. **`runtime.js` (Lifecycle)**: handles the WASM engine initialization lazily and centrally. `WebGeoDS.Runtime.python()` downloads and instantiates the environment only on the first call; subsequent calls always return the same instance, without paying the startup cost again.
2. **`python.js` (Execution)**: encapsulates `pyodide.runPythonAsync()` plus stdout capture (`setStdout`) in a single call (`WebGeoDS.Python.run(code)`) — every Python cell on the site reuses it, instead of reimplementing stdout handling each time.
3. **`code-cell.js` (Interface)**: draws the toolbar and CodeMirror-based writing area. It delegates execution to the `onRun` callback, which receives the code and the `output` object (`CellOutput`) ready to show status/result without DOM boilerplate.
4. **`map.js` (Visualization)**: initializes the map and receives the data generated by the computation — `setGeoJSON` handles both the initial creation and subsequent updates with the same call, never throwing errors on repeated Runs.

**Note on `WebGeoDS` on this page**: no waiting/polling. `map.js`, `code-cell.js`, and `runtime.js` are synchronous scripts included in a fixed order via `include-in-header`, so `window.WebGeoDS` is already complete by the time OJS starts evaluating the cells. If in the future you decide to load these scripts asynchronously (e.g. only on pages that actually need them), the waiting cell will need to be reintroduced — but with a maximum number of attempts, not a `while` loop with no exit: otherwise a network failure leaves the spinner stuck forever instead of showing a clear error.
